description: We are a multidisciplinary team interested in technology, data, and space exploration. Our skills include web development, data analysis, AI, and UI/UX design. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to combine our different skills to build a practical and user-friendly solution using NASA’s open data.
summary:
Imagine preparing to send humans to the Moon or Mars. Before taking that big step, wouldn't it be better to test things here on Earth first?

That's exactly what inspired us to create **TerraNova**.
NASA needs places on Earth that share similarities with the environments of the Moon and Mars, where scientists can experiment, learn, and prepare for future space missions. But finding these places isn't always easy.

So, we decided to make that search easier. Using data provided by NASA, we built a website powered by machine learning and artificial intelligence to explore and compare environments on Earth with those of the Moon and Mars. Through our model, we were able to identify ten potential locations on Earth that share similar characteristics.

We also wanted to make this experience more than just numbers and data, so we created an interactive website where people can explore planets and discover the results in a more engaging way.

We chose this challenge because it brings together our different skills and interests, and we wanted to turn our curiosity about space into something useful for the future of space exploration.
details:
Project Details

TerraNova is an interactive platform designed to help researchers discover locations on Earth that resemble the environments of the Moon and Mars. It combines scientific data, machine learning, and 3D visualization to make the process of identifying potential analog sites easier and more accessible.

The platform allows users to explore Earth, the Moon, and Mars through an interactive 3D interface. Users can select a planetary environment, explore relevant locations, and learn how different regions on Earth compare to extraterrestrial environments.

At its core, TerraNova uses a machine learning model to analyze and compare environmental characteristics, including terrain, surface features, climate, and soil-related data, to identify and rank potentially similar locations on Earth. The platform also includes an AI-powered chatbot that explains the results in simple language, helping users understand why a particular location is considered a potential analog and what makes it scientifically interesting.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

  • Helps researchers identify potential terrestrial analog sites more efficiently.
  • Supports preliminary research and testing before conducting experiments in lunar or Martian environments.
  • Makes scientific information easier to understand through interactive visualizations and AI-assisted explanations.
  • Encourages exploration of the relationship between Earth's environments and extraterrestrial landscapes.

Technologies and Tools:

  • Frontend: React, JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.
  • 3D Visualization: Three.js for interactive planetary environments and GSAP for animations.
  • Backend: Python for data processing and machine learning integration.
  • Machine Learning: Python-based data analysis and a similarity-based model for comparing environmental characteristics.
  • Data Visualization: Interactive maps, planetary models, and visual representations of comparison results.

Creativity and Innovation:

What makes TerraNova different is the way it brings scientific analysis and exploration together. Instead of presenting researchers with only datasets or static reports, it provides an immersive experience where users can explore planetary environments, discover potential analog locations, and interact with an AI assistant that explains the scientific results.

Our team considered scientific relevance, data availability, environmental similarities, usability, and accessibility when designing the platform. We aimed to create a solution that connects machine learning with an engaging visual experience while keeping the scientific process understandable and useful.

Ultimately, TerraNova aims to support future lunar and Martian exploration by making the discovery of Earth-based analog environments more accessible, interactive, and efficient.
